Working entry (chk-sfluluth, Epoch 2 — Debts of 0.1.0–0.3.0): «Driver debts — `press` with Ctrl, `graph --part N` as
ruled, coverage under a stopped bubbling dispatch; each the founder's fork (v040-05)». The entry carries no freight
block (`block` view: 0 rows for chk-sfluluth).

Three driver debts that 0.1.0–0.3.0 left as residuals, each brought to the founder as a fork and then either fixed and
proven on the stand through the driver's carriers, or kept as a residual by his word with his reason (intent §4,
`fct-jfc5jccy`; capability `v040-05`):

1. **`press` with Ctrl** — residual `res-hfvjj77l` (absorbed → v040-05): `press` holds no Ctrl, so a non-adjacent
   `multiple` select set cannot be built through the driver, a limit its `help` states. Kept at 2026-10-31-engine-debts
   on the founder's «Ограничение и residual (Рекомендую)» (that chunk's snapshot
   `chunks/2026-10-31-engine-debts/inputs/I12-engine-debts-founder-2026-10-31.md.txt`, line 31). Its fork now: whether
   to add a Ctrl (and, by kin, Meta/Alt) modifier to `press` beside `--shift`, and on which carriers, or keep the
   limit.

2. **The UI graph read in parts** — residual `res-7cc5bi4k` (absorbed → v040-05): `graph` takes no argument and
   answers the whole screen at once, 293,869 bytes on Cells at boot (measured at 2026-11-07-ui-graph), held only by the
   1,048,576-byte answer bound. Its FORM is already ruled: `graph --part N`, paged as `snapshot` is, the argument on the
   ratified crossing — the founder's «A. graph --part N (Рекомендую)», relayed at the 2026-11-08-handler-coverage wrap
   (`chunks/2026-11-08-handler-coverage/inputs/I7-relay-1.md.txt`). The capability's acceptance: every part within
   the answer bound.

3. **Handler coverage under a stopped bubbling dispatch** — residual `res-4dr3wt62` (absorbed → v040-05): the reached
   record writes each element of a dispatch's chain whose current listeners hold its event, and a `stopPropagation` is
   not read, so an ancestor's handler the dispatch stopped short of can read exercised — a stated limit of
   `handler_coverage` and `escher-session coverage` (`docs/capabilities.md:279-281`, pinned by dioxus-native-dom's
   reached tests). Its fork: read the stop in the reached record (fix), or keep the stated limit.

- The founder decides each debt's fix-or-keep; this chunk plans every option's cost first and puts the forks to him as
  one file (`founder-forks.md` in the run dir), relayed by the operator — the operator's directive at this take-up.
  Technical forks that change nothing of what the product is are the operator's.

- A fix crosses no new carrier: `press`'s modifier and `graph`'s `part` would be new arguments on the ratified verbs,
  on the session socket's call, the command line, MCP and a kept check — the ruling of 2026-10-10 makes a new argument

- [inferred] The answer bound (1,048,576 bytes) and `MAX_PART` (1000) bound a graph part as they bound a snapshot part.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-20-driver-debts · **Version:** escher-0.4.0

This chunk closes three driver debts of 0.1.0–0.3.0, each fixed on the founder's own word (`inputs#I2`: F1 A ·
F2 A · F3 A, every one the recommended option of `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-20T18-56-36-phase/founder-forks.md`).

1. **`press --ctrl`** (`res-hfvjj77l`). `press` gains an optional bare flag `ctrl`, held as the host's action key:
   ⌘ (Meta) on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere. That is the same per-host key the driver already holds for `select_all`
   (execute.rs:800-802) and the engine reads (`util.rs:8-10`; `(architecture · decision/platform-action-modifier)`).
   On a focused `multiple` select, `press --ctrl` on an arrow moves the current row without changing the choice, and
   a plain `press space` then flips that row (keyboard.rs:254-290). So a set of rows that are not adjacent becomes
   reachable through the driver.

2. **`graph --part N`** (`res-7cc5bi4k`). The graph is read in parts, paged as `snapshot` is: the founder's ruling,
   confirmed. The page size is `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` (10,000 bytes). `states` ride in part 1 only, and the help says
   a later part's empty `states` means "read part 1". A part answers `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…],"part":n,"parts":m}`.
   These three details are the operator's word (`inputs#I1`). A graph within the budget with no part asked answers
   whole, as today.

3. **Coverage under a stopped dispatch** (`res-4dr3wt62`). The reached record still resolves its ids before the
   handlers run, but writes them after the dispatch:
   - every listener, when nothing stopped the event;
   - only the innermost, when something did;
   - the target alone for a non-bubbling event, which Dioxus delivers to its target alone
     (`(architecture · contract/dom-events/non-bubbling)`; dioxus-core 0.7.10 runtime.rs:478-500).
   So coverage can no longer read a handler "exercised" that a stop kept the event from. What remains is the cautious
   error: when an ancestor stops the event, the listeners between it and the target may read "unexercised" although
   they ran.

`--ctrl` and `--part` are new arguments on carriers already ratified: the session socket's `call`, the command line,
MCP and a kept check. They are boundary widenings under `rul-izni57qv`, ratified by the founder's own answer
(`inputs#I2`). F3 changes no carrier, verb, argument, field, span or engine behaviour: the record is switched on only
in driver sessions and coverage runs (`(architecture · decision/dioxus-event-path-records-opt-in)`).

1. **`press`'s modifier, in the schema** (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs`, `PRESS`).
   - Add a third `ArgSpec` after `shift`: name `ctrl`, `ArgKind::Flag`, not required. Its help says it is whether the
     host's action key is held while the key is pressed: ⌘ (Meta) on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere; false when absent.
   - Rewrite `PRESS.help`'s last clause. In place of «while a set of rows that are not adjacent needs Ctrl, which this
     verb does not carry», state that with `ctrl` the arrows, `home` and `end` move the current row without choosing,
     and `space` then flips it in or out of the set.
   - Update the pinned arg table and help strings in `schema_tests.rs` (schema_tests.rs:115, :229).

2. **`press`'s modifier, typed and run** (`command.rs`, `execute.rs`).
   - `Command::Press` gains `ctrl: bool`, read in the `("press", …)` arm exactly as `shift` is (command.rs:204-206);
     its unit cases follow (command.rs:420-434, :501, :665-743).
   - `execute.rs` `press(harness, key, shift, ctrl)` builds its modifiers as `SHIFT` when `shift`, joined with the
     existing `ACTION_MODIFIER` when `ctrl`. Both callers thread it (research §Graph impact: `press` @ execute.rs:330 in
     `type_step`, passing `false`; @ execute.rs:350 in `press_key`, passing the command's `ctrl`). `Command::Press` is
     built with `ctrl: false` in `fixture_tests.rs`.
   - The command line, MCP listing, `actions` and the kept-check reader take the flag from the schema row with no code
     of their own (cli.rs:303, mcp/listing.rs:79, actions.rs:125; research §Patterns). Their tests move:
     - `cli_tests.rs`: a `--ctrl` argv case, the usage line's ` [--ctrl]`, a repeated `--ctrl` refused
       `Repeated("ctrl")`;
     - `mcp_tests.rs`: the listing's `ctrl` property `boolean`.

3. **`graph`'s part, in the schema** (`schema.rs`, `GRAPH`).
   - `args` gains one optional `ArgSpec` `part` of `ArgKind::Part`, its help as `snapshot`'s part help reads.
   - `fields` gains `part` and `parts`, each written only when read in parts, as `snapshot`'s two are.
   - `GRAPH.help` and the `states` field's help add, in so many words: a graph over the snapshot budget is read in
     parts of whole nodes; part 1 carries the whole `states` list; a later part's empty `states` means "read part 1",
     not "no states" (`inputs#I1`, the operator's note).
   - The pinned rows move in `schema_tests.rs`. `describe.rs`'s self-description follows from the table; its pinned
     counts move where a count changes (argument rows).

4. **`graph`'s part, typed and cut** (`command.rs`, `execute.rs`, `json.rs`).
   - `Command::Graph` becomes `Command::Graph { part: Option<u32> }`, read like `snapshot`'s `part` (command.rs:217,
     :312).
   - `execute.rs` `graph(harness, seen, part)` (execute.rs:438):
     - reads the whole graph and records every node id, as today, whatever part is asked;
     - with no `part` and the whole answer's written form at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` bytes, answers
       `Outcome::Graphed` whole, unchanged;
     - otherwise cuts the nodes, in their order, into consecutive parts whose written form, including `part` and
       `parts`, stays within the budget. Part 1 carries the whole `states` list, every later part an empty one. A
       node that cannot fit alone with its part's other content is a part alone;
     - answers part `part`, part 1 when none is asked, or empty `nodes` and `states` for a part past the last, with
       `part` and `parts` (`(architecture · contract/snapshot-verb/part)` mirrored).
   - Add a new `Outcome` arm for a graph part, beside `Outcome::Part`. `json.rs` writes it
     `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…],"part":n,"parts":m}` through the existing graph writer, the answer's own JSON writer
     alone (`(architecture · decision/answers-written-by-own-json-writer)`). The written form is unit-tested in
     `json_tests.rs`.
   - The command span records `verb` alone for a graph part, never the part number or count
     (`(obs-plan · contract/command-span/snapshot-part)`, mirrored).

5. **The reached record reads the stop** (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/reached.rs`, the bridge in
   `dioxus_document.rs` 465-505).
   - `ReachedRecord` splits its write in two. First it resolves, before the dispatch, the chain's elements whose
     current listeners hold the event, as ids (today's `record` body, the borrow released before the render). Then it
     writes them after `runtime.handle_event` returns:
     - every resolved entry when `event.bubbles` and `dx_event.propagates()` still reads true;
     - the first resolved entry alone when the event bubbles and `propagates()` reads false;
     - for a non-bubbling event, the entry of the first chain node holding a `data-dioxus-id` alone, when it holds
       the listener (the element `handle_event` targets, dioxus_document.rs:467-470).
   - The module doc and the `record` doc state the new rule and the remaining limit. `coverage.rs`'s module doc
     (coverage.rs:12) states it too.

6. **Unit tests** (keeps tests S3 and S4: inline, controlled red-before-green, expected values literal).
   - `reached.rs` gains `a_dispatch_its_target_stops_records_the_target_alone` (an inner `onclick` that calls
     `stop_propagation` under an outer `onclick`).
   - It also gains `a_dispatch_an_ancestor_stops_records_the_innermost_alone`, pinning the remaining limit. In it,
     three nested `onclick`s, the middle one stopping, read the innermost alone.
   - It also gains `a_non_bubbling_event_records_its_target_alone`.
   - The existing `a_bubbling_dispatch_records_its_ancestors_listener_of_the_same_event` and
     `a_bubbling_dispatch_drains_its_target_then_its_ancestor` stand unchanged: no stop, every listener.
   - Bridge cases go in `dioxus_document_tests.rs` only if a reached case there moves.

7. **Stand checks, both layout modes** (keeps tests S1 and S2: one target per file, both modes, bundled font, no
   skip). Each new test is controlled by a one-shot `gate.py control` (Test Commands).
   - `stand_act_select.rs` — `a_press_with_ctrl_builds_a_set_of_rows_that_are_not_adjacent`, on the existing
     `fx-rows` fixture (stand_act_select.rs:272-276). Focus the select and choose row 1. Then `press --ctrl` with
     `arrow-down` twice, then `press space`. The snapshot reads rows 1 and 3 selected and row 2 not. The diff names
     the chosen rows; the same calls with no `ctrl` choose row 3 alone.
   - `stand_graph.rs` — `cells_reads_in_parts_each_within_the_budget_and_together_the_whole_graph`, on Cells:
     - `graph` with no part answers part 1 of `parts` > 1;
     - every part's written form is at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`;
     - part 1 alone carries the six states, later parts `[]`;
     - the parts' nodes concatenated equal the whole graph's nodes;
     - a part past the last answers empty nodes and states;
     - `part` 0 and 1001 are refused `malformed` with nothing run;
     - a small screen (counter) with no part answers `{"nodes","states"}` whole.
     The pinned `the_whole_cells_answer_is_within_the_answer_bound` (stand_graph.rs:411) is rewritten to read the
     parts, and the «a graph with an argument is refused malformed» case is re-pointed to an unnamed argument (`id`),
     still refused.
   - `stand_handler_coverage.rs` — `an_enter_the_cell_editor_stops_leaves_the_grids_keydown_unexercised`, on Cells.
     Build a kept check of: `click` a cell (its `onclick` opens the editor, cells.rs:474), then `press --key enter`
     (the editor's `onkeydown` calls `stop_propagation`, cells.rs:508-511, under `cells-grid`'s `onkeydown`,
     cells.rs:417). `handler_coverage` over that check lists `cells-grid` `keydown` unexercised; at HEAD it reads
     exercised. The editor's own `keydown` reads exercised.
   - `stand_mcp_tools.rs` — the `press` tool's `ctrl` and the `graph` tool's `part` round-trip over MCP. A paged graph
     result is its JSON line, as a paged snapshot's is.
   - `stand_replay.rs` — a kept `graph` step with `part` replays and holds; `recording_tests.rs` keeps it, `part` in
     schema order.
   - seven_guis `cli_commands.rs` — `press --ctrl` and `graph --part 2` through the binary on Cells and a `multiple`
     select's served screen where one stands; else Cells' paged graph alone and the `--ctrl` argv in `cli_tests.rs`.
     `graph --part 0` exits 1 `malformed`, nothing written back.
- none
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — `press`'s `ctrl` arg and help; `graph`'s `part` arg, fields and help
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` — the pinned arg tables and help strings
- `packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs` — `Command::Press { ctrl }`, `Command::Graph { part }`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` — `press`'s modifiers; `graph`'s cut and its part outcome
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs` — a graph part's written form
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json_tests.rs` — the graph part's written form
- `packages/escher-driver/src/describe.rs` — the self-description's pinned counts where they move
- `packages/escher-driver/src/cli_tests.rs` — `--ctrl` and `graph --part` argv and usage cases
- `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp_tests.rs` — the listing's `ctrl` and `part` properties
- `packages/escher-driver/src/fixture_tests.rs` — `Command::Press` with `ctrl: false`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/recording_tests.rs` — a kept paged graph step
- `packages/escher-driver/src/coverage.rs` — its module doc's stated limit
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/reached.rs` — resolve before, write after, reading the stop; its tests
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` — the bridge's two record calls around `handle_event`
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document_tests.rs` — a reached bridge case, only where one moves
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_graph.rs` — Cells read in parts
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_select.rs` — a non-adjacent set through `press --ctrl`
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_handler_coverage.rs` — the grid's keydown unexercised under the editor's stop
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_tools.rs` — the two new arguments over MCP
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs` — the two new arguments through the binary
- `docs/capabilities.md` — the three limits closed or narrowed
- `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` — only where a pinned count moves
The gates are:
- the unit tests of the two library crates;

- the blitz-tests targets the steps write, plus their companions: the replay, spans, masks, actions, cross-OS
  readings and select interaction;
- seven_guis' process checks;
- the capability-statement pin;
- the pre-push gate (`fast`);

- the `doc` leg, because public doc comments change (`reached.rs`'s and `coverage.rs`'s module docs, the
  `ReachedRecord` docs) and `fast` runs no rustdoc (`(test-plan · decision/doc-leg-gates-public-doc-edits)`);
- `stand-repeat`.

No boot-path touchpoint changes a binary's start: `host_log`, `mcp_log`, `mcp_server` and `cli_commands` drive both
roles and stand in for the smoke. There is no live leg, and the cold-agent pipe is not run. The a11y leg is not
listed: this chunk changes no keyboard path of the engine. `--ctrl` sends a modifier the engine already reads, and
`stand_act_select` runs in `stand-repeat`.

Each new check is controlled red-before-green (tests S3). After the steps are green, /implement makes four one-shot
`gate.py control` runs, never entries:

- **`ctrl` held as nothing.** In `execute.rs` `press`, drop the `ACTION_MODIFIER` join. Fired on the first blitz-tests
  entry, case `a_press_with_ctrl_builds_a_set_of_rows_that_are_not_adjacent`.

- **The graph never cut.** In `execute.rs` `graph`, answer `Outcome::Graphed` whole whatever the size. Fired on the
  first blitz-tests entry, case `cells_reads_in_parts_each_within_the_budget_and_together_the_whole_graph`.

- **The stop not read, unit.** In `reached.rs`, write every resolved entry whatever `propagates()` reads. Fired on the
  unit entry, case `a_dispatch_its_target_stops_records_the_target_alone`.

- **The stop not read, stand.** The same edit, fired on the first blitz-tests entry, case
  `an_enter_the_cell_editor_stops_leaves_the_grids_keydown_unexercised`.

Each control names the edit's text and the case by its test name, `--no-fail-fast` reaching it (gate-contract.md
§Control).

The diff is OS-sensitive: `--ctrl` resolves through the `cfg(target_os = "macos")` `ACTION_MODIFIER` (execute.rs:797-802),
⌘ on macOS. So the operator's hygiene, push and CI entries stand, the CI read witnessing `stand_act_select`'s
`--ctrl` test on the macOS aarch64 and windows x86_64 legs of `matrix_test`.

body:
- (arch) `press` takes the optional flag `ctrl`, held as the host's action key. On the stand's `fx-rows` `multiple`
  select, choose row 1, then `press --ctrl` `arrow-down` twice, then `press space`: the snapshot reads rows 1 and 3
  selected and row 2 not, in both layout modes. The same calls with no `ctrl` choose row 3 alone
  (`stand_act_select` `a_press_with_ctrl_builds_a_set_of_rows_that_are_not_adjacent`; `inputs#I2` F1 A; matrix#v040-05)

- (arch) `graph` takes the optional `part` (1 to 1000). On Cells, `graph` answers part 1 of `parts` > 1, each part's
  written form within `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` (10,000 bytes, and so within the 1,048,576-byte answer bound), with
  `states` in part 1 alone. The parts' nodes concatenated equal the whole graph's, a part past the last is empty,
  `part` 0 and 1001 are refused `malformed`, and a small screen with no part answers whole. Shown in both layout
  modes, over the session in process, MCP (`stand_mcp_tools`), the command line (`cli_commands`) and a kept check
  (`stand_replay`) (`stand_graph` `cells_reads_in_parts_each_within_the_budget_and_together_the_whole_graph`;
  `inputs#I1`, `inputs#I2` F2 A; matrix#v040-05)

- (arch) `graph`'s help and its `states` field's help state that a later part's empty `states` means "read part 1"
  (`schema_tests.rs` pins the text; `inputs#I1`)

- (tests) A dispatch whose target stops it records the target alone, and one an ancestor stops records the innermost
  listener alone. A non-bubbling event records its target alone, and an unstopped bubbling dispatch records every
  listener, as before (`reached.rs` unit tests; `inputs#I2` F3 A)

- (tests) On Cells, a kept check of a cell `click` then `press --key enter` makes `handler_coverage` list `cells-grid`
  `keydown` unexercised, the editor's own `keydown` exercised, in both layout modes; at HEAD the grid's reads exercised
  (`stand_handler_coverage` `an_enter_the_cell_editor_stops_leaves_the_grids_keydown_unexercised`; matrix#v040-05)

- (security) Neither new argument reaches a log: a graph part's command span records `verb` alone and no part number
  or count. No answer echoes a typed value; the masks hold on the new answers (`stand_act_spans`,
  `stand_masks_on_new_answers`, `host_log`, `mcp_log`; `(obs-plan · contract/command-span/snapshot-part)` mirrored)

- (docs) `docs/capabilities.md` no longer states that `press` holds no Ctrl or that `graph` is not paged, and states
  the narrower coverage limit; the capability pin reads OK (`python3 .github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py`)

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast`, `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` and
  `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh stand-repeat` return 0, and the operator pass's CI read of the final HEAD reads
  `verdict: green`

- The founder's word: `inputs#I2` (F1 A · F2 A · F3 A). The operator's technical word: `inputs#I1`. The forks:
  `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-20T18-56-36-phase/founder-forks.md`.

- Research files inspected: `packages/escher-driver/src/{schema,command,execute,cli,actions}.rs`,
  `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp/listing.rs`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/{util.rs,node/text.rs,events/keyboard.rs}`,
  `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/{reached,dioxus_document}.rs`, dioxus-core 0.7.10 `runtime.rs` and `events.rs`,
  `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_graph.rs`, `examples/seven_guis/src/{session_host.rs,tasks/cells.rs}`,
  `docs/capabilities.md`.

- `--ctrl` as the literal Control key on every host — rejected by the founder (F1 B). A text field on macOS reads ⌘,
  so a recorded check would read differently by OS.
- `click --ctrl` / `click --shift` — not built (F1 C, not chosen). `click` keeps its one `id` argument.

- An exact reached record through a change inside dioxus-core — rejected (F3 C). The workspace takes no git dependency
  and no patched crate (CLAUDE.md, Critical Warnings), and Dioxus is held at the 0.7 line.

- Writing the reached record wholly after the dispatch — rejected. Its ids are resolved before the handlers run, so
  a handler that removes its own element still counts (`(architecture · decision/reached-record-before-dispatch)`).
- A part number, a part count or a part's size as a span field — never (`(obs-plan · contract/command-span/snapshot-part)`).
- A new verb, cause, session error, node key, exit status or carrier — none. The two arguments ride existing verbs.

- Cells' graph at HEAD: 293,869 B, 740 nodes, median and largest node 423 B, 6 states 1,058 B (research
  §Measurements, the built `escher-session graph` on `cells` at `1455525f`). Predicted parts at a 10,000-byte budget
  about 30 — record what the stand check measures; the check asserts `parts` > 1 and each part within the budget,
  never a count.

- `ACTION_MODIFIER` already stands in `execute.rs` under `cfg(target_os = "macos")` (execute.rs:797-802); reuse it,
  adding no new `cfg` site.

- `type_step` calls `press` (execute.rs:330) for its select-all and delete keys; it passes `ctrl: false` and its
  behaviour is unchanged.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture — `contract/driver-verbs/press` and `contract/escher-session/press` (no
  longer «carrying no Ctrl»; `--ctrl` bare, the host's action key); `contract/command-line/verb-flags` (`--ctrl`
  bare beside `--shift`); `contract/graph-verb/unpaged`, `contract/graph-verb/arguments`, `contract/graph-verb/argument`,
  `contract/driver-graph/argument`, `contract/driver-verbs/graph`, `contract/escher-session/graph` (`part` 1 to 1000,
  read in parts at the snapshot budget, states in part 1); `contract/argument-kinds/part` (a snapshot or graph part);
  `contract/handler-coverage/bubbling`, `decision/reached-record-before-dispatch`,
  `decision/reached-recorded-before-handlers` (resolved before, written after, the stop read). Pattern `rul-izni57qv`
  (boundary widening: `--ctrl` on `press`, `--part` on `graph`), answered by the founder's own word, relayed by the
  overseer (`inputs#I2`).

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan — `decision/graph-answer-unpaged` (now paged, ratified),
  `contract/driver-verbs/graph`, `contract/graph-answer/nodes-states` (a part's `part` and `parts`), a new
  `contract/cli-flags/ctrl` beside `contract/cli-flags/shift`, `decision/reached-handler-record-without-log` (written
  after the dispatch). Pattern `rul-izni57qv`, the founder's own word (`inputs#I2`).

body:
7. **Stand checks, both layout modes** (keeps tests S1 and S2: one target per file, both modes, bundled font, no
   skip). Each new test is controlled by a one-shot `gate.py control` (Test Commands).
   - `stand_act_select.rs` — `a_press_with_ctrl_builds_a_set_of_rows_that_are_not_adjacent`, on the existing
     `fx-rows` fixture (stand_act_select.rs:272-276). Focus the select and choose row 1. Then `press --ctrl` with
     `arrow-down` twice, then `press space`. The snapshot reads rows 1 and 3 selected and row 2 not. The diff names
     the chosen rows; the same calls with no `ctrl` choose row 3 alone.
   - `stand_graph.rs` — `cells_reads_in_parts_each_within_the_budget_and_together_the_whole_graph`, on Cells:
     - `graph` with no part answers part 1 of `parts` > 1;
     - every part's written form is at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`;
     - part 1 alone carries the six states, later parts `[]`;
     - the parts' nodes concatenated equal the whole graph's nodes;
     - a part past the last answers empty nodes and states;
     - `part` 0 and 1001 are refused `malformed` with nothing run;
     - a small screen (counter) with no part answers `{"nodes","states"}` whole.
     The pinned `the_whole_cells_answer_is_within_the_answer_bound` (stand_graph.rs:411) is rewritten to read the
     parts, and the «a graph with an argument is refused malformed» case is re-pointed to an unnamed argument (`id`),
     still refused.
   - `stand_handler_coverage.rs` — `an_enter_the_cell_editor_stops_leaves_the_grids_keydown_unexercised`, on Cells.
     Build a kept check of: `click` a cell (its `onclick` opens the editor, cells.rs:474), then `press --key enter`
     (the editor's `onkeydown` calls `stop_propagation`, cells.rs:508-511, under `cells-grid`'s `onkeydown`,
     cells.rs:417). `handler_coverage` over that check lists `cells-grid` `keydown` unexercised; at HEAD it reads
     exercised. The editor's own `keydown` reads exercised.
   - `stand_mcp_tools.rs` — the `press` tool's `ctrl` and the `graph` tool's `part` round-trip over MCP. A paged graph
     result is its JSON line, as a paged snapshot's is.
   - `stand_replay.rs` — a kept `graph` step with `part` replays and holds; `recording_tests.rs` keeps it, `part` in
     schema order.
   - seven_guis `cli_commands.rs`, through the binary:
     - `graph --part 2` on Cells answers one uncoloured line `{"nodes","states","part","parts"}`, status 0, and
       `graph --part 0` exits 1 `malformed`, nothing written back. `press --ctrl` is accepted on Cells' focused grid,
       status 0; no served task holds a `multiple` select, so the non-adjacent set is proven in process and over MCP
       above;
     - the coverage role on the stopped dispatch: `start cells` with `--record` into a check-owned `0700` directory,
       a cell `click`, `press --key enter`, `stop`, then `escher-session coverage cells` on the check it recorded. Its
       line lists `cells-grid` `keydown` unexercised
       (`an_enter_the_cell_editor_stops_leaves_the_grids_keydown_unexercised_through_the_coverage_role`, unix-gated as
       the recording checks are, keeps tests S5).

**Chunk:** Driver debts — press with Ctrl, graph in parts, coverage under a stopped dispatch, each fixed or kept by the founder's word
**Date:** 2026-11-21
**Run:** 2026-11-21T06-09-05-implement

- **Files:** `packages/escher-driver/src/{schema,schema_tests,command,execute,json,json_tests,cli_tests,mcp_tests,fixture_tests,recording_tests,coverage}.rs` · `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/{reached,dioxus_document}.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{stand_graph,stand_act_select,stand_handler_coverage,stand_mcp_tools,stand_replay,stand_act_spans}.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs` · `examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs` · `docs/capabilities.md` (22 files; basis `gate.py scope`: changed 22)

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - `escher_driver::Command::Press` gains the field `ctrl: bool`; `escher_driver::Command::Graph` becomes `Command::Graph { part: Option<u32> }` (was a unit variant) — public enum, every in-repo builder and matcher moved (`fixture_tests.rs`, `command.rs` units, `execute.rs`).
  - `escher_driver::Outcome::GraphPart { graph: UiGraph, part: u32, parts: u32 }` — a new public arm beside `Outcome::Part`; written by `Outcome::to_json` as `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…],"part":n,"parts":m}`. `Outcome::Graphed` stays for a whole graph. Exhaustive matchers outside the crate moved: `session_common::act`, `stand_act_spans::acting`.
  - Schema rows: `PRESS.args` gains `ctrl` (`ArgKind::Flag`, optional; help: the host's action key, ⌘ (Meta) on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere); `PRESS.help`'s last clause now states `ctrl` moves the current row and `space` flips it, the «needs Ctrl, which this verb does not carry» clause gone. `GRAPH.args` gains `part` (`ArgKind::Part`, 1 to `MAX_PART` 1000); `GRAPH.fields` gains `part` and `parts` (`always: false`); `GRAPH.help` and the `states` field's help state the paging and that a later part's empty `states` means read part 1. `MAX_PART`'s doc names the graph. No verb, cause, session error, node key or exit status added; `VERBS` holds fifteen.
  - `execute.rs` (crate-private): `press(harness, key, shift, ctrl)` joins `ACTION_MODIFIER` (Meta on macOS, Control elsewhere, the existing `cfg` site) when `ctrl`; `type_step` passes `false`. `graph(harness, seen, part)` records every node id, answers `Graphed` when no part is asked and the whole answer is at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` (10,000 B), else cuts with `graph_parts` (whole nodes, part 1 carrying the states, a node over the budget a part alone, a graph with no node one part) under the frames `GRAPH_WHOLE_FRAME` 24 and `GRAPH_PART_FRAME` 61; a part past the last answers empty nodes and states. `json::graph_lengths` (crate-private) gives each node's and the states' written lengths, the one writer measured.
  - Command line, MCP listing, `actions` and the kept-check reader take both arguments from the schema rows with no code of their own: usage line ` [--ctrl]` and `graph [--part <part>]`; MCP `ctrl` a `boolean`, `part` an `integer` 1–1000.
  - `dioxus-native-dom` (crate-private): `ReachedRecord::record` split into `ReachedRecord::resolve` (before the dispatch: the chain's elements whose current listeners hold the event, by node and id → `Resolved`) and the write after it through `ReachedRecord::pending` → `PendingWrite`, whose `finish(propagates)` writes every resolved entry when a bubbling dispatch still propagates, the innermost alone when it was stopped, and for a non-bubbling event the target alone; dropped without `finish` (a handler's panic unwinding out of `Runtime::handle_event`) it writes the dispatch as stopped. The bridge (`DioxusDocument`'s dispatch to the vdom) keeps the target node it found the `data-dioxus-id` on. Public surface unchanged (`record_reached`, `reached_handlers`, `take_step_reached`).
  - Test helpers (`session_common`): `press_ctrl`, `graph_part`, `graph_of_part`; `graphed` reads a paged graph whole (every part, part 1's states).
- **Crates / modules:** none added or removed; `escher-driver` and `dioxus-native-dom` changed.
- **Dependencies:** none.

- **Schema / config:** the driver verb table's `press` and `graph` rows (above); a kept check now may hold `press` with `ctrl` and `graph` with `part`, its `format` unchanged (1). No log field, span field or scrub set changed: a graph part's `command` span records `verb` alone (`stand_act_spans`, `stand_mcp_tools`).
- **Spec-master edits:** none.

- **Retired:** the stated limits «`press` holds no Ctrl …», «An unpaged graph» and «a `stopPropagation` is not read» in `docs/capabilities.md`, `PRESS.help` and the reached/coverage module docs (no census row).

- **Counts / qualifiers moved:**
  - escher-driver argument rows across the verb table 11 → 13 (`execute.rs` unit `the_span_has_eight_fields_and_none_is_an_argument_name`).
  - `press` arguments 2 → 3; `graph` arguments 0 → 1, result fields 2 → 4 (`schema_tests.rs`).
  - `stand_act_spans` driven calls per mode 40 → 41.
  - the capability statement's three limits narrowed or removed; its pinned counts unchanged (`test_capability_statement.py` OK, no edit).
  - Cells' graph at boot reads more than one part at the 10,000-byte budget (the stand check asserts `parts > 1`, no count).
- **Dev-tool versions:** none.
- **Harness / gate surface:** none (no CI step, leg or script changed).

- **Cross-project / external claims:** `inputs#I1` (the operator's technical word on paging: 10,000 B budget, states in part 1 alone, help saying a later empty `states` means read part 1, a part's JSON the graph keys + `part`, `parts`) and `inputs#I2` (the founder's F1 A · F2 A · F3 A, relayed). dioxus-core 0.7.10 `runtime.rs` read from the cargo registry (research): the vdom bubbles itself and returns after the first listener that stops; `Event::new(data, bubbles)` sets `propagates` from `bubbles`; a listener's panic unwinds out of `handle_event`.
- **Reverted / negative API facts:** the reached write placed plainly after `runtime.handle_event` (first firing) lost a panicking handler's record — replaced by the drop guard within this run.
- **Insufficient fixes (written, kept, not the remedy):** none.

- **Spec claims disproved by measurement:**
  - Plan step 7 / acceptance (arch): «The same calls with no `ctrl` choose row 3 alone» — measured, the plain arrows choose row 3 alone and the closing `press space` flips it out, so the plain sequence ends with no row chosen (`stand_act_select` `a_press_with_ctrl_builds_a_set_of_rows_that_are_not_adjacent`, both modes).
  - Plan step 7 / acceptance (tests): «a kept check of a cell `click` then `press --key enter`» — measured, a click opens the editor unfocused, so Enter never reaches it; the kept check needs a `click` on `cell-input` between them (both checks).
  - Research §Mechanism (the coverage fix «reachable in the bridge alone» by writing after the dispatch) — a handler's panic unwinds past the write; a drop guard is required.

- **Expected amendments (from plan):**
  - architecture `contract/driver-verbs/press`, `contract/escher-session/press` — carried: Symbols (`ctrl`, ⌘ on macOS).
  - architecture `contract/command-line/verb-flags` — carried: `--ctrl` bare beside `--shift`.
  - architecture `contract/graph-verb/unpaged`, `contract/graph-verb/arguments`, `contract/graph-verb/argument`, `contract/driver-graph/argument`, `contract/driver-verbs/graph`, `contract/escher-session/graph` — carried: Symbols (`part` 1–1000, parts at the snapshot budget, states in part 1).
  - architecture `contract/argument-kinds/part` — carried: a snapshot or graph part (`MAX_PART` doc).
  - architecture `contract/handler-coverage/bubbling`, `decision/reached-record-before-dispatch`, `decision/reached-recorded-before-handlers` — carried: resolved before, written after, the stop read, and a panic's unwind written as stopped (the drop guard — a fact the plan did not list).
  - security-plan `decision/graph-answer-unpaged`, `contract/driver-verbs/graph`, `contract/graph-answer/nodes-states`, a new `contract/cli-flags/ctrl`, `decision/reached-handler-record-without-log` — carried (Symbols; Schema / config).

Each acting verb is one settled step: snapshot, step, the load wait over `Harness::settle`, snapshot, diff — so since 2026-10-20-load-wait the five acting verbs wait on a load in flight, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, on every carrier (in process, the socket, the command line and MCP), while `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint`, `graph`, `actions` and `layout`, which run no step, wait on nothing. A refused call leaves the snapshot and both focus readings as they were.

- `Outcome` — `Screen { text }` · `Part { text, part, parts }` (since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts) · `Acted { settled, busy, diff }` · `Advanced { settled, busy, diff, advanced_ms }` · `Scrolled { settled, busy, diff, in_view }` · `Shot { width, height, png }` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) · `Linted { findings: Vec<Finding> }` (since 2026-10-19-visual-lint) · `Graphed { graph: UiGraph }` (since 2026-11-07-ui-graph, dioxus-native-dom's `UiGraph`, the whole graph) · `GraphPart` (one part of whole nodes with its `part` and `parts`, the states in part 1 alone and a part past the last empty) · `Actions { nodes: Vec<ActionNode> }` (since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here; `ActionNode { id, owner: Option<String>, keyed: bool, verbs: Vec<VerbReading> }` and `VerbReading { verb: &'static str, cause: Option<Cause> }`, both re-exported from the private module `actions`); a `layout` call answers the `LayoutExplanation` `Session::layout` reads (since 2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers); `diff` is dioxus-native-dom's `SnapshotDiff`, unchanged. An instance that did not go quiet, or an acting step whose settle panicked a second time (read as `render`), is a result (`settled: false` with its `Busy` class), never a refusal and never a `SessionError`; the step is not rolled back. `advanced_ms` is exactly the `ms` asked: the clock's move, not what a counter inside the app gained, and a step's diff can be non-empty on any animated page (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18).

- Written forms — `Outcome::to_json`, `Refusal::to_json`, `SessionError::to_json`: one line of JSON each, keyed by the schema's own words, output only. An outcome is an object keyed by its verb's result fields in the table's order (`busy` only when not settled, `caused` only when the step caused something and `caused_past` only when entries pass `caused`'s 16); a node is keyed by `NODE_FIELDS` in order — fifteen keys: `id` · `parent` · `role` · `name` · `enabled` · `checked` · `value` · `selected` · `pressed` · `invalid` · `focused` · `clickable` (since 2026-11-07-ui-graph: true where the element's current listeners hold `click` and it is no disabled form control) · `highlighted` (since 2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts: true on an open single select list's highlighted option alone, read from the accessibility tree's active descendant) · `bounds` · `differs` (since 2026-10-12-self-description; written on a changed node only, after `bounds`: the node-key words whose reading differs from before the step, a node that only moved reading `bounds` alone, an added node written without it) — with `parent`, `enabled`, `checked`, `value`, `selected` and `pressed` left out when absent, `highlighted` written only when true, `invalid` and `clickable` always written, each a boolean on every node, `bounds` four numbers; a refusal is `{"refused":{"cause","meaning","remedy"[,"fault"]}}`; a session error `{"error":{"kind","message","remedy"}}` (the remedy since 2026-10-12-self-description); a `screenshot`'s outcome `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot), the PNG's base64 written by hand in the private `image::base64` (RFC 4648 §4, padded) — no base64 crate taken; a `lint`'s outcome `{"findings":[…]}`, each finding keyed `id` · `defect` · `bounds` (`[x, y, width, height]`, as a node's bounds), then its reason's keys — `other` and `area` for an overlap, `visible` for a clip, `text` then `visible` (left out when no part can be seen) for a truncation, `ratio` (its shortest decimal, `null` when not finite) and `required` for contrast, none for off-screen and zero-size; a `graph`'s outcome `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}` (since 2026-11-07-ui-graph), a part's `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…],"part":n,"parts":m}` with `states` in part 1 alone — a node keyed `id` · `owner` · `component` · `handlers` · `reads`, `owner` and `component` left out when absent, a handler `event` · `writes`, a write `state` · `declared` · `confirmed` · `flag`, `flag` left out when none; a state keyed `name` · `component` · `declared` · `writers` · `readers`, `component` left out when absent, a declaration `id` · `event`, a writer `id` · `event` · `declared` · `confirmed` · `flag` — ids, component, state and event names, closed flag words, booleans and the part counts only, never a value; an `actions` outcome `{"nodes":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"keyed":…,"verbs":[{"verb":…,"cause":…}]}]}` (since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here), written by the crate-private `json::action_node`, `owner` and `cause` left out when absent, a cause by `Cause::name` — ids, owner ids, the table's verb words, closed cause words and booleans only, never a value, typed text or `NodeId`; a `layout` outcome `{"id","bounds","laid_out","placed":{"by","container"?,"canvas"?,"at","relative"?},"shifts":[{"by","holder"?,"dx","dy"}],"width","height"}` (since 2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers), each size `{"px","by","size","min","max","flex"?}` — ids, closed words and numbers only; a paged `snapshot`'s outcome `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}`, a whole screen's still `{"text":…}` alone; `start` answers `label`, `pid`, `idle_expiry_s`, `status` adds `served`, `stop` answers `{"stopped":true}`.

the sixth, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07), `screenshot` (one optional `id`; result `width` (count), `height` (count) and `png` (`FieldKind::Png`, base64 text), all always present; the seventh, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, its help stating one measured limit — an element shot is cropped to the part of its bounds that can be seen — the overlay scrollbar fade reading the session's clock, so two shots of one state with no `advance` between them read the same pixels (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18)), `lint` (the eighth, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint: no argument, one named refused `malformed` with `Fault::Unnamed`; result `findings`, `FieldKind::Entries`, always present; its help stating the six defect words, each reason's keys and its limits — geometry only, no hit, right-to-left and vertical text read as left-to-right lines), `graph` (the ninth, since 2026-11-07-ui-graph: one optional `part` (1 to 1000), anything else refused `malformed` with nothing run; result `nodes` (`FieldKind::GraphNodes`) and `states` (`FieldKind::GraphStates`), plus `part` and `parts` when read in parts, the screen's UI graph whole when within the snapshot budget and no part is asked), `actions` (the tenth, since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here: no argument, an argument refused `malformed` with `Fault::Unnamed`; result `nodes` (`FieldKind::ActionNodes`), what each actionable node can take now, its help pinned word for word), `layout` (the eleventh, since 2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers: one required `id`; result `id`, `bounds`, `laid_out`, `placed`, `shifts`, `width` and `height`, each always present), then `start` (`app`), `status` and `stop` (session-level; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10), then `help` (tool-level, no argument; result `verbs` · `node_keys` · `key_names` · `busy_classes` · `causes` · `exit_statuses` · `session_errors`, each field with its help; since 2026-10-12-self-description, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12); each a `VerbSpec { name, level, help, args, fields }`; `verb(name)` finds one by its exact name only. Argument kinds and bounds (`ArgKind`): `id` 1 to `MAX_ID_BYTES` (1024) bytes of text · `text` 0 to `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` (4096) bytes · `key` one of the twelve `KEY_NAMES` · `flag` · `milliseconds` 1 to `MAX_MILLISECONDS` (60000) · `name` 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-` · `part` a whole number 1 to `MAX_PART` (1000), `snapshot`'s and `graph`'s, the seventh kind. The acting verbs' result: `settled` (its help stating the load wait's bound, «a load in flight waited for up to 5 s», since 2026-10-20-load-wait), `busy` (one of `BUSY_CLASSES`, only when not settled), `added`, `removed`, `changed` (nodes carry the `NODE_FIELDS`), and, since 2026-11-16-errors-with-the-action, `caused`, present only when the step caused something: an item per panic, error or record — its kind, level, source, target, message cut at 1024 bytes, location, an error's boundary and chain, a log's fields, its `error` field kept, and the first reached handler — panics, then errors new since the boundary marks, then records, 16 kept, a caught panic the capture's hook did not see still answering a `panic` item whose message is the fixed text `<payload unread>`, and `caused_past`, written after `caused` only when non-empty, one entry per kind and source counting the items past `caused`'s 16, a panic or error entry writing no source; `advance` adds `advanced_ms`, `scroll` adds `in_view` (always present); `help`'s fields are of the kinds `Words` · `Entries`, and `screenshot`'s `png` of `Png` (base64 text, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) , and `graph`'s `nodes` and `states` of `GraphNodes` (`graph-nodes`) and `GraphStates` (`graph-states`), and `actions`' `nodes` of `ActionNodes` (`action-nodes`), sharing `graph`'s field name and not its kind — and `layout`'s readings of the rect, placement, shifts and size kinds among the `FieldKind`s. The help of `changed` and of `snapshot`'s `text` say the state words and the two limits of the boolean model — a mixed toggle reads unpressed (`pressed` false), a grammar or spelling error reads invalid — so an agent learns them from the tool; since 2026-10-12-self-description `NODE_FIELDS` is `[NodeFieldSpec; 15]`, each row `NodeFieldSpec { name, help }` whose help states the key's reading — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's own state, else the toggle of the five checkable roles (`aria-checked`), a mixed one reading false, `selected` · `pressed` · `invalid` read by `aria-selected` · `aria-pressed` (left out for those five roles) · `aria-invalid`, the two limits among them — and the crate docs' one sentence says each limit is stated in its node key's help and that a changed node names the keys whose reading differs (`differs`).

- `validate(call: &Call) -> Result<Command, Refusal>` — a `Call` is a verb name and named `ArgValue`s (`Text` · `Number` · `Flag`); it receives no `Session`, so a refused call changes nothing. One answer per call, the first failure in this order: the verb by exact name (`unknown-verb`; a session-level verb and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help` too), then the call's arguments in the order passed (a name the verb lacks, a name passed twice), then the verb's arguments in the schema's order (missing, wrong kind, outside its bound) — the last five are `malformed` with a `Fault` naming the rule. `Command` is `Snapshot { part: Option<u32> }` (a `part` admitted in `1..=MAX_PART` through `u32::try_from`, any other number `OutOfBound`, a text or a flag `WrongKind`) · `Click` · `Type` · `Press` · `Advance` · `Scroll` · `Screenshot { id: Option<String> }` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) · `Lint` (validated from `("lint", [])`, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint) · `Graph` (validated from `("graph", [])` or with one `part` from 1 to 1000, since 2026-11-07-ui-graph) · `Actions` (validated from `("actions", [])`, since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here) · the `layout` call's command (validated with its one required `id`, since 2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers), and `Command::spec()` is its verb's row. `validate_session(&Call) -> Result<SessionCommand, Refusal>` is the same check over the three session-level rows and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help` — an instance-level verb `unknown-verb` there, an argument to `help` `malformed` with `Fault::Unnamed` (`SessionCommand`: `Start { app }` · `Status` · `Stop` · `Help`, `Help`'s spec `HELP`).

- `command_line(args, apps, boot) -> ExitCode` — the whole command line of a binary that boots apps (`boot` an `FnMut` since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface); it installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable. The reader's rules, in order: no first word → usage; `serve <app> --session <dir>` in exactly that shape or with one `--record <dir>` after it, else usage; `mcp` alone or with one `--record <dir>`, else usage (since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface; `--record` since 2026-10-19-session-recording); since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage `coverage <app> <check>...` in that one shape — an app the binary boots, then one or more kept-check paths, no `--session` and no `--record` word among them — else usage, each path read through `File::open(..).take(MAX_CHECK_BYTES + 1)`, then `Check::from_bytes`, a file that cannot be read, one past the bound, one that is no check and a check whose `app()` is not `<app>` refused `malformed`, status `1`, holding nothing of the path or the file, accepted the coverage line on stdout, status `0`, a boot that fails the session error, status `3`, the role calling the binary's boot once per check through `handler_coverage`; a `--record` anywhere else, twice or with no value is usage once the call passed `validate`; `help` with no argument and at most one `--session <dir>`, which is not read, answers `describe()`'s line on stdout, status `0`, reaching no session — `help` with an argument is refused `malformed`, `1`, and `--session` with no directory or given twice is usage, `2` (since 2026-10-12-self-description); a first word the verb table does not hold → the refusal `unknown-verb`; the call the remaining words spell (flags as the schema spells them — `--id`, `--text`, `--key`, `--ms` and `--part` each with one value, `--ms`'s and `--part`'s read as a number, `--shift` and `--ctrl` bare; `start`'s app as one plain word) is checked by `validate` or `validate_session` before the session address is asked for; then `--session <dir>` exactly once, else usage; `start` on an app the binary does not boot → usage. Four endings: accepted — the answer on stdout, status `0`; refused — the refusal on stdout, `1`; usage — one fixed line on stderr built from `VERBS` and the app names, `2`; session error — the error object on stdout and its message on stderr, `3`; the host role ends quiet, status `0`; the `mcp` role hands stdin and stdout to `serve_mcp` with `IDLE_EXPIRY` and writes nothing on stdout at its end — `0` on `Ok`, `3` with the error's fixed message on stderr on `Err` — and the usage line names it (`; mcp role: mcp [--record <dir>]`, then `; coverage role: coverage <app> <check>...;` before `; apps:`), with `snapshot [--part <part>]`, `graph [--part <part>]` after `lint`, press's `[--ctrl]`, `layout --id <id>` after `actions`, `start <app> [--record <dir>]` and `host role: serve <app> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]`; `start --record` and `mcp --record` check the recording directory first, a refusal ending status `3` with nothing spawned or served. No command's ending writes back anything the caller typed, but `caused` carries an app's own messages and fields as their author wrote them, `error` included, scrubbed by the answer's own hidden field names, so an app that writes typed text into a record echoes it. `start` spawns the running binary again as `serve <app> --session <dir>`, with `--record <dir>` after it when it was given one, its streams closed, waits up to 30 s for it to answer, and neither kills nor reaps it.

- The wire (`wire.rs`, crate-private, versioned `v3`, `v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording) is one request line and one reply line per connection: `hello v3` → `ok v3 pid= label= served= idle_expiry_s=`, `stop v3` → `ok v3 stopping`, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` → `ok v3 accepted <json>` · `ok v3 refused <json>` · `ok v3 oversize` · `ok v3 recording-failed` (sent in place of the answer when the host's recording ended after the call, the client reading it as `RecordingFailed`), another version of a known word → `refused version`, anything else → `refused malformed`. Kinds are `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value are percent-escaped byte for byte and decoded strictly. A request is bounded at 16,384 bytes, a lifecycle reply at 128, an answer at 1,048,576 on its JSON line; each read and write at 2 s, a client's read of an answer at 30 s. **What the screen reads crosses it in an answer** — ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the mask), the snapshot's text and the diff — and an element id and typed text cross in (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10); no `NodeId` crosses. Inside the text and the diff an element that states one also reads selected, pressed or invalid — closed words in the text, booleans in a diff node, never an attribute's value as typed: an inventory fact of the ratified crossing, not a further widening (the founder, 2026-10-10), who set the rule with it — a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening; authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is. The MCP surface was that next crossing question: since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the same content crosses to an MCP client in tool results over the `mcp` role's stdio, the request-id echo and the bounds above ratified by the founder with it (2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»); the next surface that carries any of it is a new crossing question — since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the operator-driven live cold-agent run carries the stand's screen (element ids, accessible names and control values in snapshot texts and diffs, layout, graph and actions answers, and acting answers' caused text, the order page's authored messages among it, from this MCP server) on to the model provider, one run, on the founder's «Один запуск, до $3 (Рекомендую)» and «JSON-проверка с повтором (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-15). - A driver call is checked by `escher_driver::validate` — a session-level one (`start` · `status` · `stop`) or the tool-level `help` by `validate_session` — before anything runs: a closed verb table of fifteen verbs in three levels (`screenshot`, the seventh asked of the held instance, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, `lint`, the eighth, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint: no argument, one result field `findings`, running no step, and `graph`, the ninth, since 2026-11-07-ui-graph: an optional `part` from 1 to 1000, anything else refused `malformed` with nothing run, result fields `nodes` and `states` (a graph within the 10,000-byte snapshot budget with no part asked one whole answer, else parts of whole nodes each within the budget, a part adding `part` and `parts`, the states in part 1 alone, a part past the last empty — a ratified boundary widening), running no step — a ratified boundary widening onto every ratified carrier, and `actions`, the tenth, since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here: no argument, any argument refused `malformed` with nothing run, one result field `nodes`, running no step — a ratified boundary widening onto every ratified carrier, and `layout`, the eleventh, since 2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers: one required id, refused `malformed` without it or with a second argument and `not-found` or `stale` for an unknown id, changing nothing, delivered Timer ticks left unapplied, answering the element's placement, shifts and sizes as ids, closed words and numbers), seven argument kinds with bounds (`part`, the seventh since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts, the one optional argument of `snapshot` and of `graph`, a whole number from 1 to 1000, `MAX_PART`), one fixed refusal order, no panic path on what a call supplies, and no `Session` in its signature — so a refused call changes nothing. A refusal is one of eight causes with fixed texts (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18; `fonts-unavailable` since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) and holds nothing of the call; a reach error is likewise one of a closed set (unknown state, refused at a step with the step's index and its closed refusal cause, or not settled at a step with the busy reading), each a fixed text holding nothing a caller supplied; keep it that way (no id, name, value or call-supplied argument name in a `Refusal`, a `Fault`, a test name or an assertion message). A fixture state name is compared whole against the app's closed table of named states before any session starts; any other name is refused as an unknown state and nothing is booted. The schema is executed by `escher_driver::Session::run`, which validates first, and since 2026-10-10-driver-cli it is reached from outside the process by three surfaces, each through `validate` before anything is sent or run: the socket's `call` request, which a host runs through `Session::run` and nothing else, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface an MCP `tools/call`, whose arguments of the wrong JSON kind are refused `malformed` before the server runs it through `Session::run` (session verbs through `validate_session`), and the `escher-session` command line (`escher_driver::command_line`) — a closed argv reader whose usage line, refusals and session errors write back nothing the caller typed, and whose stdout is the command's answer (ids, names, values and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a shot's base64 PNG and a lint's findings by the ratified crossing), never a log line; an acting driver command waits on a load in flight for at most `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time, re-settling every 10 ms, moving no time on the held instance, then `settled: false` with its busy class; since 2026-10-20-load-wait), and `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint`, `graph` and `actions` wait on none; the session's layout read, in process or through the `layout` verb on any ratified carrier, resolves its id through the run path's id resolution (refusing `stale` or `not-found`), runs no step, pump, tick or settle, and answers stable id strings, closed words and numbers, never a `NodeId`, text or value. The session keeps a record of id text to tell `stale` from `not-found` (at most 4096 ids, none longer than `MAX_ID_BYTES`, session-lived, private): never a `NodeId` in it, never print, log or field it. Since 2026-10-19-visual-lint `Session::lint` also feeds it from its own snapshot, and `Session::actions` with every id it reads; it takes no argument and returns `Finding`s holding ids, closed defect words and numbers only (no `NodeId`, page text, colour or control value) and crosses as the `lint` verb's answer (`Command::Lint` → `Outcome::Linted`, written `{"findings":[…]}`) on every ratified carrier — the socket's `call`, the command line, MCP and a kept check, kept whole — a ratified boundary widening, with no log site, print, span or field carrying a finding and `VERBS` holding fifteen. An `Outcome` holds ids, names and values and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a shot's PNG bytes (`Outcome::Shot`) and a lint's findings (`Outcome::Linted { findings }`: stable ids, closed defect words and numbers only) and a screen's part (`Outcome::Part { text, part, parts }`, the snapshot text's own lines, written `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}`) and a UI graph (`Outcome::Graphed { graph: UiGraph }`, written `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}`, a part adding `part` and `parts` with its states empty past part 1, its node ids also feeding the session's record of ids) and an actions answer (`Outcome::Actions { nodes }`, written `{"nodes":[…]}`: ids, owner ids, `keyed` booleans, verb words and closed cause words) and, on an acting verb's answer (`click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`) only when the step caused something, `caused` on every ratified carrier: one item per panic, boundary error and kept record, holding its message (what its author wrote, no mask applying), location, boundary, cause chain and fields, its `error` field as its author wrote it within the text bound, every other content-named field read as redacted (a boundary widening to the error text, ratified), prints them under `Debug` and is written as JSON by `to_json` alone — as a command's answer, or as an MCP tool result's text — never log or field one; a handler `Err` the app's root error boundary takes crosses as screen content, through Dioxus's default boundary rendering of its Display, and in `caused` as one error item holding its message and cause chain under the root boundary. The driver's log records are two spans: the command span of `Session::run` (`escher_driver` / `command`), eight fields of fixed schema words, bools and counts, of a refusal its cause's name only, and since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the `tool_call` span of an MCP tool call, its parent, holding `tool` and `ending` only, both closed words (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10) — add no field that holds what a call supplied or a screen reads — the screen text or its length, a part's number or the part count, a shot's image, its size or its dimensions, a lint's findings or their count included a graph's ids, component, state and handler event names and an actions answer's ids, owner ids, verb words and causes a layout answer and a step's caused text, from a driver call or an in-process read, included (a `screenshot`, a `lint`, an `actions` call or a part read records `verb` and, refused, `cause`; a `graph` call, a graph part's included, or a `layout` call records `verb` and, refused, `cause`, never the part asked or the part count).
